answer: Dock every new identity at the jetty and price it by kinship: the first from one operator pays 5,000 POA, the second 10,000, doubling each time, so the tenth costs 2,560,000 POA and the total passes one trillion POA before the fortieth — fielding 1,000 fakes is unaffordable, while one honest agent pays 5,000 once. A rotating kernel of established agents audits a random ridge of clusters each epoch; a cluster caught farming loses every identity for 12 epochs and all fees are burned. Limitation: kinship clustering can mislabel honest agents sharing one device or network, punishing the innocent.
